satellites.name: Landsat 8
satellites.status_note: USGS mission-page snapshot; no live service check.
satellites.purpose: Long-term land-surface change and thermal observations.

orbit.temporal_note: 16-day single-platform repeat; 8-day offset with Landsat 9. Clouds reduce usable optical observations.

sensors.name: OLI
sensors.spectral: 9 bands, visible to SWIR including cirrus

products.name: Collection 2 Surface Reflectance
products.note: Atmospherically corrected surface reflectance; inspect QA bands.

sensors.name: TIRS
sensors.spatial: 100 m native thermal; distributed on a 30 m grid

products.name: Collection 2 Surface Temperature
products.note: Retrieved surface skin temperature; resampling does not add spatial detail.

satellites.name: Landsat 9
satellites.status_note: USGS mission-page snapshot; no live service check.

sensors.name: OLI-2 + TIRS-2
sensors.spatial: OLI-2: 15 m pan / 30 m multispectral; TIRS-2: 100 m native

products.name: Collection 2 SR / ST
products.note: Reflectance and temperature are different physical quantities.

satellites.name: Sentinel-2B
satellites.status_note: Nominal B/C pair reported by SentiWiki.
satellites.purpose: Frequent multispectral mapping of land and coastal areas.

orbit.temporal_note: 10-day single-platform repeat; nominal B/C pair: 5 days. Cloud-free revisit varies.

products.name: MSI Surface Reflectance
products.note: Bottom-of-atmosphere reflectance; distinguish from L1C TOA reflectance.

satellites.name: Sentinel-2C
satellites.status_note: Replaced Sentinel-2A in the nominal pair on 2025-01-21.
satellites.purpose: Maintain continuity of Sentinel-2 multispectral observations.

orbit.temporal_note: 10-day single-platform repeat; nominal B/C pair: 5 days.

products.name: MSI Surface Reflectance
products.note: Check platform-specific spectral response and processing baseline.

satellites.name: Sentinel-1C
satellites.status_note: Operational since May 2025 according to SentiWiki.
satellites.purpose: Day/night radar imaging for land, ocean and ice monitoring.

orbit.temporal_note: 12-day single-platform orbital repeat. Actual acquisition frequency depends on observation plan.

sensors.name: C-SAR
sensors.spatial: IW: 5 x 20 m single-look; product pixel spacing differs
sensors.spectral: C-band radar; polarization and mode dependent

products.name: IW SLC / GRD
products.note: SLC preserves phase for interferometry; GRD is detected, multilooked intensity.

satellites.name: ALOS-2
satellites.status_note: JAXA observation-plan snapshot; regional radio-interference restrictions noted in May 2026.
satellites.purpose: L-band radar monitoring of land, forests and disasters.

orbit.temporal_note: 14-day repeat; acquisition, steering and observation plan govern actual coverage.

sensors.name: PALSAR-2
sensors.spatial: Spotlight 1 x 3 m; stripmap 3-10 m; ScanSAR 100 m

products.name: PALSAR-2 observation archive
products.note: Registration and product-specific access terms apply.

satellites.name: EnMAP
satellites.purpose: Imaging spectroscopy of ecosystem and mineral properties.

orbit.temporal_note: 27-day repeat; 4-day revisit capability with +/-30 degree off-nadir pointing is not guaranteed acquisition.

sensors.name: EnMAP imaging spectrometers
sensors.spectral: 420-2450 nm; sampling about 6.5 nm VNIR / 10 nm SWIR

products.name: EnMAP surface reflectance
products.note: Access via mission archive; quality and atmospheric correction matter.

satellites.name: EO-1 / Hyperion
satellites.status_note: Mission powered down 2017-03-30. ARSET reports last hyperspectral data 2017-02-22; these dates describe different events.
satellites.purpose: Historical imaging-spectroscopy technology demonstration and archive.

orbit.temporal_note: Historical targeted archive; repeat and altitude not curated here. No current observations.

sensors.name: Hyperion
sensors.coverage: Targeted historical scenes; not continuous global coverage

products.name: Hyperion L1 radiance archive
products.note: Level 1 is radiance. Atmospheric correction is required before surface-reflectance analysis.

satellites.name: Fengyun-3D
satellites.status_note: NSMC lists FY-3D and MERSI-II as operational in the source snapshot.
satellites.purpose: Meteorology and land, ocean and ice monitoring.

orbit.temporal_note: 14:00 ascending equator crossing; revisit not curated. Do not infer it from orbit height.

sensors.name: MERSI-II (selected payload)
sensors.coverage: Global meteorological mission; swath not curated

products.name: FY-3D MERSI L1
products.note: 250 m and 1 km radiometrically calibrated products; pair with correct geolocation.

satellites.name: EOS-06 / Oceansat-3
satellites.status_note: Mission and archive documented; current spacecraft service status not independently curated.
satellites.purpose: Ocean colour, sea-surface temperature and wind continuity.

orbit.temporal_note: NRSC describes 2-day coverage of India by OCM; this is coverage, not a curated orbital repeat. Altitude not curated.

sensors.name: OCM-3 (selected payload)
sensors.spatial: 360 m archive product; check coverage mode
sensors.coverage: Wide-area coverage; NRSC reports India coverage in 2 days

products.name: EOS-06 OCM archive
products.note: Product level and processing depend on the selected collection.

satellites.name: GOES-19
satellites.status_note: Designated GOES East on 2025-04-07; designation is not a check of present instrument availability.
satellites.purpose: Rapid weather and environmental imaging over the Americas.

orbit.temporal_note: ABI mode 6: full disk 10 min, CONUS 5 min, two mesoscale domains 60 sec. Scan cadence is not orbital revisit.

sensors.name: ABI (selected payload)
sensors.spatial: 0.5 / 1 / 2 km at sub-satellite point, band dependent
sensors.coverage: Full disk centred on 75.2 W; resolution degrades toward limb

products.name: ABI L1b radiance / L2+ products
products.note: Derived products have their own grids, quality flags and validity domains.

satellites.name: Meteosat-12
satellites.status_note: WMO OSCAR lists operational status and FCI L1C service since 2024-12-04.
satellites.purpose: Rapid imagery over Europe, Africa and adjacent oceans.

orbit.temporal_note: FCI full-disk imagery every 10 minutes. Cadence differs from LEO orbital repeat.

sensors.name: FCI (selected payload)
sensors.spatial: 1-2 km normal full-disk channels at nadir
sensors.spectral: 16 channels; high-resolution service uses a subset
sensors.coverage: Earth disk centred near 0 degrees; off-nadir pixels enlarge

products.name: FCI L1c imagery
products.note: Do not assign high-resolution subset sampling to all 16 channels.

satellites.name: Himawari-9
satellites.status_note: JMA lists operational observations; primary role began 2022-12-13.
satellites.purpose: Rapid weather imaging over East Asia and the western Pacific.

orbit.temporal_note: AHI full disk 10 min; Japan and target regions 2.5 min. Availability varies with operations.

sensors.name: AHI
sensors.spatial: 0.5 / 1 / 2 km at sub-satellite point, band dependent
sensors.coverage: Earth disk centred on 140.7 E; off-nadir pixels enlarge

products.name: Himawari Standard Data
products.note: Check distribution service, calibration and usage conditions.

applications.name: Philadelphia heat vulnerability
applications.historical_platform: Historical Landsat thermal imagery; the study predates Landsat 8 and 9. Those platforms are modern teaching analogues only.
chain: Spatial linkage to neighborhood socioeconomic factors and heat deaths
applications.design: Spatial observational analysis; Philadelphia, 1993 heat event; remotely sensed thermal context and socioeconomic indicators related to heat-related mortality.
applications.finding: The study examined how remotely sensed heat patterns supplement socioeconomic indicators of vulnerability; it is not an intervention trial.
applications.limitations: Land-surface temperature is not personal exposure or air temperature; spatial association does not establish causation. NCEH coauthorship does not imply every related study is NCEH-led. No patient data are bundled.

applications.name: Hyperspectral land management
applications.limitations: ARSET case studies include airborne AVIRIS and HyMap: neither is a satellite. Synthetic notebook spectra are illustrations, not measurements or species classifiers.

applications.name: Radar change mapping
applications.limitations: Radar backscatter is not optical reflectance. Flood identification is conditional on land cover, geometry, wind and validation; no health effect is inferred.
